explanations.explanation: Not quite, friend. Verse 1 opens with a rule about death for the priests, but verse 2 gives exceptions right away: his immediate family. So it isn't every dead person. The list is short, and God spells it out.

That's right, baker. God tells Moses that a priest is not to defile himself for a dead person among his people. Then verse 2 starts a short list of exceptions. So the opening rule is the starting point, and the exceptions are part of the picture too.

That's the one, baker. Verse 3 names his unmarried sister who is near to him, since she has no husband. She joins his mother, father, son, daughter and brother on the list. The text gives that reason, so I'll stick with it.

Close, but this one isn't on the list. Verse 3 says his unmarried sister who is near to him, "…since she has no husband." The text names the sister without a husband, and a married sister isn't mentioned. Same sister, different line on the page.

I get the thought, friend, because an uncle feels close. But the list in verses 2 and 3 doesn't include him. It names the priest's mother, father, son, daughter, brother and unmarried sister. No uncle in there, so we only count what the text counts.

Careful on this one, friend. Verse 4 says the priest is not to defile himself for those related to him by marriage, and so profane himself. The exceptions in verses 2 and 3 were blood relatives and an unmarried sister. In-laws weren't in that group, and I'll leave it right there.

Yes, baker. Verse 4 says he is not to defile himself for those related to him by marriage, and so profane himself. The family exceptions just before it were his mother, father, son, daughter, brother and unmarried sister. Relatives by marriage aren't on that list.

You've got it. Verse 5 says priests must not make bald spots on their heads, shave off the edges of their beards, or make cuts in their bodies. That's three things, and cuts are the third. I read all three and checked my own mustache twice, just to be safe.

Good guess, but face paint isn't in this verse. Verse 5 lists three things: no bald spots on their heads, no shaving off the edges of their beards, and no cuts in their bodies. Paint never comes up, so the answer is the cuts. I have exactly zero face paint in my bakery anyway.

Beard dye sounds like it fits next to the beard rule, doesn't it? But verse 5 doesn't say anything about dye. The beard part is about not shaving off the edges, and the third thing is making cuts in their bodies. Mine's still the original color, friend, if you were wondering.

explanations.answer: They present the LORD's food offerings
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. Verse 6 says they present to the LORD the food offerings, the food of their God, and that's why "They must be holy…" Think about handing someone a cookie box for a big celebration. I'm wiping the chocolate off my mustache first. Handling something that belongs to God is a much bigger deal than that.

explanations.answer: They were born first in their families
explanations.explanation: I see why you'd go there, friend, but verse 6 never says anything about birth order. It gives one reason: they present to the LORD the food offerings, the food of their God. That's what the holiness is tied to. When the text hands us the reason, we take it.

Nice try, baker, but this verse doesn't say where the priests live. The reason in verse 6 is that they present to the LORD the food offerings, the food of their God. Their holiness is tied to what they present. Where they sleep isn't part of it.

Yes, baker. In verse 8 God says the priest shall be holy to the people, "…because I the LORD am holy…" He adds that He is the One who sets them apart. The holiness starts with who God is, and it all flows from there.

This one is true, friend. Verse 8 says the people are to regard the priest as holy, since he presents the food of their God. Then God says, "He shall be holy to you, because I the LORD am holy…" It's easy to miss because the verse sounds like a lot of rules, but God gives His own holiness as the reason.

Careful, friend. This is where the highest priest is different. Regular priests had the family exceptions in verse 2, but verse 11 says he must not go near any dead body. He must not defile himself, even for his father or mother. The question tells you the setup, and the answer is a stricter rule.

That's right, baker. Verse 11 says the highest priest must not go near any dead body, and he must not defile himself, even for his father or mother. For regular priests, mother and father were on the exception list in verse 2. His rule is stricter, and I think that's a hard one.

explanations.answer: The anointing oil of his God is on him
explanations.explanation: You've got it, baker. Verse 12 says the consecration of the anointing oil of his God is on him, and verse 10 says that oil was poured on his head. Flour on my hat only means I've been working. This oil means God set him apart. That's the reason the text gives for not leaving or desecrating the sanctuary.

explanations.answer: He keeps watch over the gold inside
explanations.explanation: That's a creative one, friend, but verse 12 doesn't mention gold or watching anything. The reason it gives is that the consecration of the anointing oil of his God is on him. That oil was poured on his head, according to verse 10. So the oil is the answer.

explanations.answer: The people need him at the gate
explanations.explanation: I can see a busy gate in my mind, baker, but the text doesn't put him there. Verse 12 says he must not leave or desecrate the sanctuary of his God, for the consecration of the anointing oil of his God is on him. The reason is the oil, not a crowd.

Not quite, friend. Verse 14 says he is not to marry a widow, a divorced woman, or one defiled by prostitution. Instead he is to marry a virgin from his own people. A widow is the first one on the "no" list, so it's easy to see why this one tricks people.

Right, baker. Verse 14 says he is not to marry a widow, a divorced woman, or one defiled by prostitution. He is to marry a virgin from his own people. That's a longer list than the one for regular priests in verse 7, which is why I called this the extended edition.

explanations.answer: So he does not defile his offspring
explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. Verse 15 says he marries a virgin from his own people so that he does not defile his offspring among his people. Then God says, "…for I am the LORD who sanctifies him." The reason comes straight from the text.

explanations.answer: So his wife can serve beside him
explanations.explanation: That sounds sweet, friend, but the text doesn't say it. Verse 15 gives the reason: so that he does not defile his offspring among his people. It adds that the LORD is the One who sanctifies him. Nothing about his wife serving appears in the verse.

explanations.answer: So his family keeps its land
explanations.explanation: Land is a reasonable thing to wonder about, baker, but verse 15 doesn't bring it up. The reason it gives is so that he does not defile his offspring among his people. God adds, "…for I am the LORD who sanctifies him." That's the whole reason on the page.

Not this time, friend. In verse 17 God tells Moses to say to Aaron that for the generations to come, none of his descendants who has a physical defect may approach to offer the food of his God. So the answer is no. This rule reaches down through the generations, so it's not just for Aaron's day.

Yes, baker. Verse 17 says that for the generations to come, none of Aaron's descendants who has a physical defect may approach to offer the food of his God. It's a rule for the long haul. I think it's a lot to take in, and that's what the text says.

That's right, baker. Verse 22 says he may eat the most holy food of his God as well as the holy food. He can't offer it, but he's still allowed to eat it. He's still one of Aaron's family, and that's the part of this passage I'd hate for you to miss.

I get why you'd think so after all those "must not" lines, friend, but this one is true. Verse 22 says he may eat the most holy food of his God as well as the holy food. The rules in verse 23 are about going near the veil and approaching the altar. They don't take away his place at the table.

explanations.answer: So he won't desecrate God's sanctuaries
explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. Verse 23 says that because of his defect, he must not go near the veil or approach the altar, so as not to desecrate My sanctuaries. Notice who is speaking there: God Himself, calling them His. Then He adds, "For I am the LORD who sanctifies them." The sanctuaries are His, and He is the one who makes them holy. That's like a friend handing you the keys to their house and saying, "Hey, treat it right." It's not your place, so you follow their rules.

explanations.answer: So the altar fire keeps burning
explanations.explanation: A fire guess makes sense next to an altar, friend, but this verse doesn't mention the fire. Verse 23 gives the reason as not desecrating God's sanctuaries. Then God adds, "For I am the LORD who sanctifies them." The answer is about the sanctuaries.

explanations.answer: So he can rest from his work
explanations.explanation: That's a kind thought, baker, and we all need a rest sometimes. But the text doesn't give rest as the reason. Verse 23 says he must not go near the veil or approach the altar, so as not to desecrate God's sanctuaries. The reason is the sanctuaries, and I won't add one that God didn't say.

explanations.answer: Aaron and his sons and all the Israelites
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. Verse 24 says Moses told this to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites. So it wasn't kept between the priests. Everybody heard it.

explanations.answer: Aaron and his sons and the elders
explanations.explanation: Close, friend, but the elders aren't named here. Verse 24 says Moses told this to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites. That's a much bigger crowd than a few leaders. The whole camp was in on it.

explanations.answer: Aaron and his sons and the Levites
explanations.explanation: The Levites make a fair guess, baker, since Numbers 3:6 has the tribe of Levi presented to Aaron the priest to serve him. But verse 24 doesn't name them. It says Moses told this to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites. That's everyone, not just one group.
